./planning/pr-faq/right-now-summary.md:7:**Kanbus introduces Right-Now Summary: a one-sentence status for every issue, the instant it changes**
./planning/pr-faq/right-now-summary.md:11:KANBUS, Sept. 2, 2026 — Kanbus today announced Right-Now Summary, a new way to understand a Kanbus board at a glance. Every time an issue changes, Kanbus rewrites that issue into a single short sentence in the style of an Apple Intelligence notification summary: terse, Hemingway-style, never longer than one line. The summaries flow into a reverse-chronological current-status feed in the web console and a new `kbs right-now` command for agents, so anyone can scan the whole board in seconds instead of opening issue after issue.

./README.md:16:Kanbus is a spiritual successor to [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads), inspired by its elegant, domain-specific approach to project management. We are deeply grateful to the Beads author and community for proving that a dedicated cognitive framework for tasks is game-changing.
./README.md:18:Kanbus builds on this foundation by adapting the model to be a thinner, more native layer over Git—optimizing for AI agents and distributed teams:
./README.md:20:* **A Thinner Layer over Git**: We removed the secondary SQLite index. The complexity of maintaining and synchronizing a shadow database isn't worth the operational cost. Kanbus reads files directly.
./README.md:22:* **Conflict-Free Storage**: Instead of a single JSON-L file (which guarantees merge conflicts when agents work in parallel), Kanbus stores separate tasks in separate files. This eliminates conflicts and allows deep linking to specific issues from GitHub.
./README.md:25:* **Git-Native Scoping**: We replaced complex "contributor roles" with standard Git patterns. Want local tasks? Just `.gitignore` a folder. Working in a monorepo? Kanbus respects your current directory scope automatically.
./README.md:29:Kanbus is designed to **remove friction**, not add it. 
./README.md:32:* **Git Hooks Help You**: Git hooks should assist your workflow, not interrupt it. Kanbus hooks are designed to be invisible helpers, ensuring data integrity without stopping you from getting work done.
./README.md:34:For a detailed comparison, see [Kanbus vs. Beads](docs/VS_BEADS.md).
./README.md:36:## Why Kanbus?
./README.md:39:Offload your mental context. Instead of keeping 15 different chat sessions and open loops in your head, tell your agent to "record the current state" into Kanbus. It's a permanent, searchable memory bank for your AI workforce.
./README.md:48:Unlike other file-based systems that use a single JSONL file (guaranteeing merge conflicts), Kanbus stores **one issue per file**. This allows multiple agents and developers to work in parallel without blocking each other.
./README.md:51:Kanbus includes a **Wiki Engine** that renders Markdown templates with live issue data. Your planning documents always reflect the real-time state of the project, giving agents the "forest view" they often lack.
./README.md:54:There are no per-seat licenses or hosted fees. If you have a git repository, you already have the database—and that keeps Kanbus affordable for very large teams (or fleets of agents).
./README.md:60:Kanbus is in production.

./README.md:188:Kanbus uses a just-in-time index daemon for read-heavy commands such as `kanbus list`. The CLI auto-starts the daemon when needed, reuses a healthy socket, and removes stale sockets before restarting.
./README.md:206:Kanbus ships two CLI implementations with identical features. Both run the same behavior specs with full coverage and share interoperability tests (including Beads), so workflows and outputs match exactly. The difference is setup and speed: Python is the lightest install path, while Rust requires Rust 1.88+ (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` for rustup and CI) but runs substantially faster.
./README.md:219:Kanbus keeps Python and Rust in lockstep: both CLIs run the same Gherkin specs, share identical JSON serialization, and target the same operational model. The duality is intentional—pick the runtime that fits your packaging or performance needs without changing workflows.
./README.md:225:We benchmarked real data from the Beads project (836 issues) to measure end-to-end “list all beads” latency, including process startup. Scenarios: Beads (Go, SQLite + JSONL), Kanbus Python/Rust reading the Beads JSONL (`--beads`), and Kanbus Python/Rust reading project JSON files. Five runs each with caches cleared between runs.
./README.md:235:Cold/Warm medians (ms, cold over warm shown as stacked bars): Go 197.6/5277.6; Python — Beads 566.1/538.7; Rust — Beads 11.9/9.9; Python — JSON 648.3/653.5; Rust — JSON 92.4/54.6. Warm runs reuse the resident daemon for Kanbus; cold runs force `KANBUS_NO_DAEMON=1` and clear caches each iteration. Go/Beads warm path spikes because its SQLite daemon import dominates the second run.

If `kbs wiki list` calls `console_wiki::list_pages`, add the existence check in `list_wiki_pages` **before** or after that call; do not silently map empty to success in the CLI match arm.\n\n## Gherkin (first)\n\nIn `features/wiki/wiki_research_kb.feature`, beside `Missing wiki directory shows create hint`, add:\n\n```\nScenario: Wiki list on a missing wiki directory shows create hint\n Given a Kanbus project with default configuration\n And the wiki directory does not exist\n When I run \"kanbus wiki list\"\n Then the command should fail with exit code 1\n And stderr should contain \"wiki directory not found\"\n And stderr should contain \"kbs wiki init\"\n```\n\nDo not weaken render/lint scenarios.\n\n## Implementation\n\n- Python `list_wiki_pages`: if not `location.wiki_root.exists()`, `raise WikiError(wiki_directory_missing_message(location))`.\n- Rust `list_wiki_pages`: same check using `load_wiki_location` / existing helper; then list as today.\n- Update **unit tests** that currently assert empty list when missing (`python/tests/test_wiki.py` `list_wiki_pages` missing case; `wiki_list_pages_empty_when_wiki_root_missing` if it tests `list_wiki_pages` rather than `console_wiki::list_pages`). If the test is on `console_wiki::list_pages`, leave it.\n- Dual runtime. Spec parity. Sphinx/rustdoc already on these functions: update the `:raises:` / `# Errors` lines.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Rewording the hint (see sibling bug kbs-8f2559f0). Use the helper as it exists.\n- Making search fail.\n- Wiki init implementation.\n\n## Quality\n\n- Smallest change. No debug. No emojis.\n- Branch `cursor/wiki-list-missing-dir-bf9f` from `develop`, push, no PR.\n\n## Proof\n\nRun the new scenario in Python behave and Rust cucumber; comment results on this issue.\n",

Conceptual fields: resource_id, owner_id, claim_id, revision, claimed_at, expires_at. Delete on complete. DynamoDB TTL for abandoned leases. Even a busy install should have dozens to hundreds of live records.\n\nTiny API: acquire, renew, release, perhaps inspect. Prototype and measure actual request cost.\n\n## Depends on\n\nProtocol Gherkin. Git and MQTT remain fallbacks when this provider is not configured.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nGherkin for acquire/renew/release/inspect and failed conditional checks; dual-runtime client; Git-only and MQTT-only installs unchanged.",

Two separate signals address diagrams:\n\n1. Suggestion: when a description or comment does not contain any diagram code block, suggest that one might be appropriate.\n2. Error: when a description or comment DOES contain a diagram code block, validate its syntax before accepting it. This already exists for some diagram types (content_validation.rs) but needs to be unified and confirmed to apply on all create/update/comment paths.\n\nScenario: Suggestion emitted when no diagram is present in a description\n\nGiven an agent creates an issue with a description that contains no fenced code block with a diagram language (mermaid, plantuml, d2)\nWhen the CLI creates the issue\nThen a suggestion is printed to stderr noting that diagrams can be embedded using fenced code blocks\nAnd the suggestion is a SUGGESTION-level message (non-blocking)\nAnd the suggestion names the supported diagram languages\n\nScenario: Suggestion emitted when no diagram is present in a comment\n\nGiven an agent adds a comment with no diagram code block\nWhen the CLI adds the comment\nThen a suggestion is printed to stderr about diagram support\n\nScenario: No diagram suggestion when a diagram is already present\n\nGiven a description or comment contains a fenced code block with language mermaid, plantuml, or d2\nWhen the CLI processes it\nThen no diagram suggestion is emitted\n\nScenario: Broken Mermaid diagram syntax is rejected with an error\n\nGiven an agent creates an issue with a description containing a fenced mermaid code block\nAnd the mermaid syntax in that block is invalid\nWhen the CLI validates the content\nThen the issue is NOT created\nAnd an error is printed to stderr identifying the broken diagram\nAnd the error message includes the diagram language and the validation failure reason\n\nScenario: Broken diagram syntax in a comment is rejected\n\nGiven an agent adds a comment containing an invalid diagram code block\nWhen the CLI processes the comment\nThen the comment is NOT saved\nAnd an error is returned identifying the diagram language and failure\n\nScenario: Valid diagram passes through without error\n\nGiven a description contains a valid mermaid flowchart\nWhen the CLI creates the issue\nThen the issue is created with no diagram-related error\nAnd no diagram suggestion is emitted\n\nScenario: --no-validate bypasses diagram validation but not the suggestion\n\nGiven an agent uses --no-validate on a comment containing a broken diagram\nThen the diagram syntax error is suppressed\nBut the suggestion about diagram support is still emitted if applicable (suggestions are never suppressed by --no-validate)",

Implement tskl-55e first.\n\n## View Toggle\n\nA new AnimatedSelector in the toolbar (or replacing the existing one) lets the user switch between two modes:\n- Board view (left option, board/grid icon)\n- Metrics view (right option, chart/bar icon)\n\nClicking Board slides the kanban board back in from the left and the metrics panel out to the right. Clicking Metrics slides the metrics panel in from the right and pushes the kanban board out to the left.\n\n## Metrics Panel Layout\n\nThe panel is wide enough to show three conceptual columns when space allows:\n\n**Left column — Summary counts**\n- A large prominent number at the top: total issue count for the current filtered view\n- Below it: breakdown rows (count per status, count per project if virtual projects exist, count by scope/source if local issues exist)\n\n**Right two columns — Stacked bar chart**\n- A landscape-oriented stacked bar chart occupying roughly two-thirds of the panel width\n- Bars represent issues grouped by a chosen dimension (e.g. status, type, project)\n- Segments within each bar are colored by status category: grey for To Do, blue for In Progress, green for Done (matching the category colors defined in .kanbus.yml)\n- A chart visualization library must be selected as part of this work — requirements: flexible, styleable to match the application design system, supports stacked bar charts, works with React\n\n## Chart Library Selection\n\nA discovery/design task should be created to evaluate and select the chart library before implementation begins. Requirements: React-compatible, fully styleable (no opinionated themes that fight the design system), supports stacked bar charts, actively maintained.\n\n## Color Mapping\n\nStatus category colors from .kanbus.yml (grey → gray Radix, blue → blue Radix, green → green Radix) are used for chart segment colors, resolved through the existing issue-colors.ts color alias system. Metadata is optional, stored in issue JSON, displayed in CLI and console only when present, and recorded in event payloads for auditability.\n\n## Problem\n\nWhen humans and multiple AI agents collaborate in Kanbus, `author: agent` and `KANBUS_USER=agent` do not distinguish Cursor from Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity, nor which model or settings produced a change. Provenance matters for debugging, policy enforcement, and multi-agent coordination.\n\n## Design decisions (resolved)\n\n| Decision | Choice | Rationale |\n|----------|--------|-----------|\n| Storage location | Top-level optional `agent` on `IssueData` and `IssueComment` | Typed, validated, avoids `custom` collisions and overlay keys |\n| Not in | `custom.agent`, `comment.data.agent`, `agent_metadata` | One way only; `comment.data` reserved for summary compaction |\n| Issue semantics | Set at create only; immutable thereafter | Avoids conflating filing agent with human triage edits |\n| Comment semantics | Optional per comment | Matches mandatory running-log workflow in comments |\n| Platform | Validated string (max 64, lowercase `[a-z0-9_-]+`) | Document canonical values; avoid enum lock-in when new tools appear |\n| Canonical platforms | `claude_code`, `codex`, `antigravity`, `cursor` | CLI autocomplete and docs; unknown-but-valid strings accepted |\n| Settings | Allowlisted keys only | `temperature` (0.0-2.0), `thinking_level` (off/low/medium/high), `max_output_tokens` (>0) |\n| Secrets | Reject keys matching api_key/token/secret/password/credential | Prevent accidental git commits of credentials |\n| Size limit | Max 2 KB serialized `agent` block | Limit repo bloat on chatty agent sessions |\n| Env defaults | `KANBUS_AGENT_PLATFORM`, `KANBUS_AGENT_MODEL`, `KANBUS_AGENT_SETTINGS` | Mirrors `KANBUS_USER`; flags override env |\n| CLI flags | `--agent-platform`, `--agent-model`, `--agent-settings` | On `create` and `comment` only (not `update`) |\n| Beads mode | Reject `--agent-*` with clear error | Beads JSONL cannot round-trip comment metadata |\n| Display | CLI `format_issue_for_display` + console `AgentMetadataBlock` | Only when `agent` present; no empty placeholders |\n\n## Data model\n\n```json\n{\n \"agent\": {\n \"platform\": \"cursor\",\n \"model\": \"composer-2.5\",\n \"settings\": {\n \"temperature\": 0.2,\n \"thinking_level\": \"high\"\n }\n }\n}\n```\n\nOmit the `agent` key entirely when absent (not `null`). Omit `settings` when empty.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TB\n subgraph input [Agent runtime]\n CLI[CLI flags]\n ENV[KANBUS_AGENT_* env]\n end\n\n subgraph validate [Write boundary]\n RESOLVE[resolve_agent_metadata]\n VALID[Validate platform model settings]\n end\n\n subgraph persist [Native Kanbus storage]\n ISSUE[IssueData.agent create-only]\n COMMENT[IssueComment.agent per comment]\n EVENTS[Event payloads snapshot]\n end\n\n subgraph display [Conditional display]\n CLIOUT[CLI show / create output]\n CONSOLE[Console detail + comments]\n end\n\n CLI --> RESOLVE\n ENV --> RESOLVE\n RESOLVE --> VALID\n VALID --> ISSUE\n VALID --> COMMENT\n ISSUE --> EVENTS\n COMMENT --> EVENTS\n ISSUE --> CLIOUT\n COMMENT --> CLIOUT\n ISSUE --> CONSOLE\n COMMENT --> CONSOLE\n```\n\n## Definition of done\n\n- Gherkin specs pass in Python and Rust\n- Python/Rust parity on validation, storage, CLI flags, display, and error messages\n- Console shows agent metadata only when present (issue header + per comment)\n- Event payloads include `agent` on `issue_created` and `comment_added` when present\n- Beads mode rejects agent flags with a clear error\n- Documentation updated in CLI reference and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md\n\n## Out of scope (follow-up epics)\n\n- `agent.session_id` deduplication across comments\n- `kbs list --agent-platform` filtering\n- Beads upstream schema proposal\n- `--json` on create/comment commands",

That is not a mutex.\n\nThe README currently says exclusive claiming was removed because it does not align with distributed Git. This initiative does **not** reverse that: Git-only installs stay fully functional, and duplicate work remains possible at Level 1. We add an optional claim/lease layer on top, with stronger guarantees only when extra infrastructure is configured.\n\n## Three levels\n\n1. **Git (required):** Durable source of truth. Soft-lease via the issue/event model. Contention windows must tolerate Git latency. A Git-only installation is legitimate, not broken.\n2. **MQTT (optional):** Kanbus already has optional MQTT gossip/overlay (`docs/REALTIME.md`). Fast-path CLAIM → contention window (seconds) → deterministic tie-break → LEASE / renew / RELEASE. Soft mutex only; partitions can still duplicate.\n3. **Mutex API (optional):** Hard arbitration. Atomically create/claim resource X iff nobody currently owns X. Proposed shape: API Gateway REST → direct DynamoDB conditional write. No Lambda. No AppSync. Workers authenticate to the Kanbus Mutex API; they do not get the AWS account. DynamoDB holds only live leases (resource_id, owner_id, claim_id, revision, claimed_at, expires_at), not Kanbus history. TTL garbage-collects abandoned leases.\n\nA worker asks Kanbus to claim a resource. Kanbus uses the strongest configured provider. Business logic does not fork per transport.\n\n## Protocol (define first, Gherkin source of truth)\n\nOne transport-independent claim/lease protocol: resource identity, owner identity, claim IDs, contention behavior, lease TTLs and renewals, expiration, release/completion, deterministic collision resolution, revision semantics, and failure behavior. Then implement Git lease → MQTT fast-path → optional hard-mutex provider. Dual-runtime (Python + Rust) after Gherkin; no Python-only or Rust-only PRs.\n\n## Revision-aware results\n\nPublication is by logical task revision, not whoever finishes last. An obsolete local render must not overwrite a newer revision. Pattern: local-first → wait → cloud backstop, without making the cloud the queue or source of truth.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nThis is not a second queue competing with Kanbus. Durable history stays in Git. DynamoDB is ephemeral coordination state only.",

./project/issues/kbs-76a4c80a-5e81-45a8-bf9c-9488d3c716bc.json:4: "description": "# PR FAQ: Right-Now Summary\n\n> Working Backwards document for the \"right-now summary\" initiative. This document is the authoritative body of the Kanbus Initiative. It is a product spec, not an implementation spec; Gherkin, Python, and Rust follow once the Initiative is approved.\n\n## Press Release\n\n**Kanbus introduces Right-Now Summary: a one-sentence status for every issue, the instant it changes**\n\n*New glanceable feed lets agents and humans see what is happening across the whole board without reading a single issue body.*\n\nKANBUS, Sept. 2, 2026 \u2014 Kanbus today announced Right-Now Summary, a new way to understand a Kanbus board at a glance. Every time an issue changes, Kanbus rewrites that issue into a single short sentence in the style of an Apple Intelligence notification summary: terse, Hemingway-style, never longer than one line. The summaries flow into a reverse-chronological current-status feed in the web console and a new `kbs right-now` command for agents, so anyone can scan the whole board in seconds instead of opening issue after issue.\n\nIssue titles are written for the future and issue bodies accumulate history. Neither is good for \"what is happening right now.\" A 4,000-word epic description tells you what the epic is for, not that the auth refactor landed yesterday and the migration is blocked on a review. Right-Now Summary closes that gap. It is computed the moment an issue changes, cached, and shown next to the title in the feed. It recurses up the hierarchy: a task's right-now summary rolls into its epic's right-now summary, which rolls into its initiative's right-now summary, so the top of the board reads like a news ticker for the whole project.\n\n\"Right-Now Summary turns a Kanbus board from a filing cabinet into a newsroom,\" said a Kanbus maintainer. \"You look at the feed and you already know the story.\"\n\nGetting started is a single command. Run `kbs right-now` for a reverse-chronological list of recently-updated issues, each with its title and its right-now summary. Add `--tree` to see initiatives at the top, epics nested beneath them, and tasks beneath those, in a collapsible tree that defaults to expanded or collapsed as you choose. In the web console, the same data powers a current-status panel that updates in real time as issues change.\n\nFor an agent triaging a board it has never seen, the feed is the difference between reading thirty issues and reading thirty sentences. For a human catching up after a day away, it is the difference between a wall of cards and a headline.\n\nRight-Now Summary is available today in Kanbus.\n\n## Tenets\n\nThese are the principles the design must not violate. They are the rules we will test against.\n\n1. **One sentence, always.** A right-now summary is one short line or sentence. Never two. Never a paragraph. If it does not fit, it is wrong, not longer.\n2. **Glanceable before complete.** The feed is for scanning, not reading. A missing or stale summary must never block the feed from rendering.\n3. **State is not prose.** The summary captures the *substance* of what is happening, never the *state label*. It must not say an issue is \"done,\" \"in progress,\" or \"blocked,\" because the status field already says that. It may shift tense (past tense for completed work) because that describes the work, not the enum.\n4. **Right-now is cheap; full is dear.** Right-now summaries run on every change and must be fast and cheap. Full summaries are expensive and run rarely, on a separate mechanism. Right-now never triggers full.\n5. **Use what exists; never wait for it.** When a parent's right-now summary is built, it uses the children's right-now summaries and any full summaries that already exist. If a child has no full summary yet, the parent reads the child's raw issue. It never asks for a full summary to be made first.\n6. **Cache, don't recompute.** A right-now summary is computed once per change and cached until the next change. The feed reads the cache.\n7. **One way, in both runtimes.** Python and Rust produce identical observable behavior for the same inputs. No fallbacks, no legacy paths.\n\n## Customer Personas\n\n**The Agent.** A long-running agent that wakes up, looks at a board it may have never seen, and must decide what to do next. It cannot afford to read every issue body. It needs the board's current story in a single CLI call it can parse: `kbs right-now`. The hierarchical tree lets it drill from an initiative's one-sentence status down to the tasks underneath without a second round of `kbs show` calls.\n\n**The Human.** A maintainer returning to a board after a day or a week. They want to know what moved, what is stuck, and what landed, without opening cards. The web console's current-status panel gives them that in a glance, updating live as the board changes.\n\n## Goals and Non-Goals\n\n### Goals\n\n- A right-now summary for every issue, one short sentence, Apple-Intelligence-notification tone, recomputed on every change to the issue.\n- A reverse-chronological current-status feed of recently-updated issues, each showing title + right-now summary, in both the CLI (`kbs right-now`) and the web console.\n- Hierarchical roll-up: a parent's right-now summary is built from its children's right-now summaries plus any existing full summaries, falling back to raw children when no full summary exists.\n- Optional collapsible tree view (Initiative > Epic > Task > Sub-task) with a configurable default expand/collapse state, in both CLI and web.\n- Full behavior spec (Gherkin) coverage of all of the above.\n- Python/Rust parity for all observable behavior.\n\n### Non-Goals\n\n- Changing the existing `kbs summarize` / `kbs lifecycle compact` full-summary machinery. That stays as the separate, expensive, infrequent tier.\n- Defining the trigger mechanism for full summaries. That is a related but distinct concern and is left as an open question.\n- Replacing issue titles or descriptions. Right-now summary is a derived, cached view, not a stored rewrite of the issue body.\n- Summarizing non-issue entities (wikis, comments in isolation). Right-now summary is per-issue.\n\n## FAQ \u2014 External\n\n**What is Right-Now Summary?**\nA single short sentence per issue that says what is happening with that issue right now, recomputed every time the issue changes. It shows up next to the title in the current-status feed.\n\n**Where does it show up?**\nIn the web console's new current-status panel and in the CLI via `kbs right-now`. Both show recently-updated issues reverse-chronologically with title + right-now summary.\n\n**Is it always available?**\nThe feed is always available. If a summary has not been computed yet (for example, a brand-new issue), the feed shows the title with the summary pending or omitted, never blank-stalling the render.\n\n**Can I disable it?**\nRight-now summary generation can be disabled via configuration (open question: exact key). When disabled, the feed still renders with titles only.\n\n**Is it stored?**\nYes. Each right-now summary is cached on the issue and invalidated on the next change to that issue. It is distinct from the full-summary cache.\n\n**Does it replace `kbs summarize`?**\nNo. `kbs summarize` produces a full summary (rewritten description + activity summary) and is the expensive, infrequent tier. Right-Now Summary is the cheap, frequent tier. They coexist.\n\n**How does it handle the hierarchy?**\nA parent issue's right-now summary is built from its children's right-now summaries and any full summaries the children already have. If a child has no full summary, the parent reads the child's raw issue instead. Right-now never asks for a full summary to be produced.\n\n## FAQ \u2014 Internal\n\n**What generates the summary?**\nAn LLM, via the same LiteLLM provider path used by the existing `summarize` machinery (see `python/src/kanbus/summarize.py`, `rust/src/summarize.rs`). Right-now uses a dedicated, tighter prompt and a smaller word budget than full summaries.\n\n**What is the exact context for a right-now summary?**\nFor a leaf issue: title + description + recent activity (comments, status transitions), bounded by a token budget. For a parent issue: the parent's own title/description/activity plus, for each child, the child's right-now summary AND the child's full summary if one exists; if no full summary exists, the child's raw issue (title + description + activity) is used instead.\n\n**Does right-now ever trigger a full summary?**\nNo. This is a hard rule. Right-now only consumes full summaries that already exist. Full summaries are produced by a separate, less-frequent mechanism (open question: the trigger).\n\n**When is a right-now summary invalidated?**\nOn any change to the issue: description edit, comment added, status change, label change, assignment change, parent/child link change. The exact event set is an open question but the default is \"any write to the issue.\"\n\n**When a child's right-now summary changes, is the parent's invalidated too?**\nYes. Because the parent's context includes the child's right-now summary, a change to a child invalidates the parent's right-now summary (and recursively up the chain, bounded by the hierarchy). The propagation rule is an open question to nail down in the spec.\n\n**Where is the right-now summary stored?**\nOpen question. Candidates: a new `comment_type` (e.g. `right_now`), a dedicated field on the issue, or reuse of the existing summary comment. The \"no backward-compat / one way\" policy means we pick exactly one and migrate, not support several. The PR FAQ recommends a dedicated storage slot distinct from the full-summary comment, but the final choice is deferred to the spec phase.\n\n**What is the word/length budget?**\nOne sentence. Open question: a hard character or word cap (e.g. <= 120 characters) to enforce \"one line\" across terminals and the web panel.\n\n**What is the recursion depth bound?**\nThe configured hierarchy in `.kanbus.yml` (`initiative -> epic -> task -> sub-task`). Right-now rolls up the parent chain to the top. Max depth is therefore the hierarchy depth. Per-level truncation of child context is an open question.\n\n**What about cost and latency?**\nBecause right-now runs on every change, cost and latency matter more than for full summaries. The design must use a small prompt and a fast model. Offline / no-provider behavior is an open question: recommended fallback is to leave the previous right-now summary in place rather than emit an error.\n\n**How is \"no state duplication\" enforced and tested?**\nThe prompt instructs the model not to restate status. Testing exact wording is brittle, so the Gherkin specs will assert structural properties (length cap, absence of status keywords, presence after a change) rather than exact strings, plus a parity check that Python and Rust agree.\n\n**How do Python and Rust stay in parity?**\nSame prompt, same context assembly, same cache key, same invalidation rules, same JSON shape for the cached summary, same CLI output formatting and ordering. Parity is verified with `tools/check_spec_parity.py` and byte-for-byte comparison where deterministic.\n\n## Open Questions\n\nThese are deferred to the spec phase (after Initiative approval). The PR FAQ takes a recommended position where noted but does not lock it in.\n\n1. **Full-summary trigger mechanism.** What produces full summaries and when? Manual `kbs summarize`? A scheduled job? An age/size threshold? A hook? Out of scope for this initiative's implementation, but must be named so the two tiers stay decoupled. Recommended: leave the existing manual + `lifecycle compact` triggers as-is.\n2. **Right-now invalidation event set.** Confirm \"any write to the issue\" means: description edit, comment, status change, label change, assignment change, parent/child link change. Define the exact set.\n3. **Parent invalidation propagation.** When a child changes, how far up the chain do we invalidate, and do we regenerate eagerly or lazily on next feed read? Recommended: invalidate up the chain eagerly, regenerate lazily on read.\n4. **Storage location.** New `comment_type`, dedicated issue field, or reuse of existing summary comment. Must reconcile with the \"no backward-compat / one way\" policy. Recommended: a dedicated storage slot distinct from the full-summary comment.\n5. **Context budget when full summaries are absent.** If many children lack full summaries, the parent reads all their raw issues. Define a token/size budget and truncation/fallback behavior. Recommended: cap total child-raw context, truncate oldest/lowest-priority children first.\n6. **Length cap.** Hard character or word limit to enforce \"one line.\" Recommended: <= 120 characters.\n7. **LLM provider/model and offline behavior.** Which model for the right-now tier, and what happens when no provider is configured. Recommended: same provider as full summaries, smaller/faster model; on failure, keep the previous summary.\n8. **Default expand/collapse for the tree view.** And whether the web panel and CLI share that default. Recommended: shared default, configurable, default collapsed except for the top level.\n9. **Determinism of \"no state duplication.\"** How to instruct the LLM reliably and how to test it in Gherkin. Recommended: structural assertions, not exact-string.\n10. **Real-time updates in the web panel.** Does the current-status panel subscribe to the existing realtime feed (MQTT-over-WSS / SSE in `apps/console/src/api/client.ts`) so summaries update live? Recommended: yes.\n\n## Appendix: Proposed CLI and UI Surface\n\n### CLI\n\n```\nkbs right-now [options]\n\nOptions:\n --limit <n> Number of recently-updated issues to show (default 30)\n --tree Show issues hierarchically (Initiative > Epic > Task > Sub-task)\n --expanded With --tree, expand all nodes by default\n --collapsed With --tree, collapse all nodes by default (default)\n --raw Show titles only, no right-now summaries (for offline / debugging)\n --json Emit machine-readable JSON for agents\n```\n\nDefault (flat, reverse-chronological) output, one row per recently-updated issue:\n\n```\n<updated_at> <id> <title>\n <right-now summary>\n```\n\nWith `--tree`, initiatives appear at the top level, epics nested beneath their initiative, tasks beneath their epic, each indented and prefixed with a collapse marker, each showing title + right-now summary.\n\n### Web Console\n\nA new **Current Status** panel in the console:\n\n- Reverse-chronological feed of recently-updated issues, title + right-now summary per row.\n- Optional hierarchical tree toggle (Initiative > Epic > Task > Sub-task), collapsible nodes, default expand/collapse from configuration.\n- Subscribes to the existing realtime feed so rows and summaries update live as issues change.\n- A right-now summary that is pending or unavailable renders as the title only; the feed never blocks.\n\n### Data flow\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n Change[\"Issue change\n (edit/comment/status/link)\"]\n Invalidate[\"Invalidate right-now cache\n for this issue + ancestors\"]\n GenLeaf[\"Generate right-now summary\n (leaf: title + desc + activity)\"]\n GenParent[\"Generate right-now summary\n (parent: own context + children\n right-now + children full-if-exists\n else children raw)\"]\n Cache[\"Store right-now summary\n (distinct from full-summary cache)\"]\n Feed[\"Current-status feed\n CLI kbs right-now + web panel\"]\n\n Change --> Invalidate\n Invalidate --> GenLeaf\n GenParent -.uses children right-now + full-or-raw.-> GenLeaf\n Invalidate --> GenParent\n GenLeaf --> Cache\n GenParent --> Cache\n Cache --> Feed\n\n FullSum[\"Full summary\n (separate, infrequent mechanism)\"]\n FullSum -.read by GenParent if present.-> GenParent\n FullSum -.never triggered by right-now.-> GenParent\n```\n\n## Status\n\nThis is a PR FAQ, not an approved plan. Filing this document as a Kanbus Initiative begins the review. Epics, Tasks, and Gherkin scenarios are written after the Initiative is approved.",

An incompatible version should fail immediately with the required version, running version, and documented upgrade command. Development builds should be handled explicitly rather than silently accepted.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- A BDD scenario covers an older CLI opening a newer project.\n- The command exits nonzero before project or realtime initialization.\n- The error names both versions and gives one supported upgrade path.\n- A compatible CLI continues normally.\n- Python and Rust CLIs behave consistently.",

./project/issues/kbs-6db7d9c7-2571-405c-9ec1-14aec07e7cf5.json:24: "text": "# Implementation plan: CLI must honor `kanbus-version`\n\nThis is the prescribed plan. Follow it. Do not invent extra product behavior.\n\n## Intent\n\nAs an operator, I want the CLI to refuse to run against a project whose `kanbus-version` is newer than the running CLI, so that installation drift is reported as a version mismatch instead of opaque I/O or schema errors.\n\n## Product contract\n\n- File: repository-root `kanbus-version` (sibling of `.kanbus.yml` / project root as resolved by existing `resolve_root`). Observed live format is a single trimmed line such as `0.19.1` or `0.20.0`.\n- Comparison is **semver core only**: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The running CLI must be **greater than or equal to** the declared requirement.\n- Git-describe / development builds (`0.18.3-29-g36a5204`, `0.19.1-5-gdeadbeef`) are handled **explicitly**: parse the leading `X.Y.Z` and treat the remainder as a pre-release/build suffix that does **not** count as satisfying a *higher* requirement. `0.19.1-5-g...` satisfies `0.19.1`. `0.18.3-29-g...` does **not** satisfy `0.19.1`.\n- If `kanbus-version` is **absent**, skip the check (current projects without the file keep working).\n- If the file exists but is empty, has multiple version tokens, or cannot be parsed as `X.Y.Z`, fail with a dedicated parse error (do not fall through to project load).\n- If the running CLI version cannot be parsed, fail with a dedicated error naming the raw version string. Do not silently accept it.\n\n## When the check runs\n\nRun **once**, immediately after CLI parse and root resolution, and **before**:\n\n- project repair prompts\n- Beads mode / issue loading\n- `validate` / schema walks\n- doctor checks\n- daemon / Mosquitto / realtime client setup\n- wiki, list, or any other project command\n\nExempt only commands that never open a project:\n\n- `--help` / `-h`\n- `--version` / `-V`\n- `init` (and Python `setup` / `repair` if they currently skip project structure for the same reason)\n\n`doctor` **must not** be exempt. A mismatch must fail doctor too.\n\nPython and Rust must share **byte-identical** error text and the same exit code (nonzero, same as other `IssueOperation` / `ClickException` failures: 1).\n\n## Error text (identical in both CLIs)\n\nUse one message, no emojis, no alternate phrasings:\n\n```\nKanbus CLI <running> does not satisfy this project's required version <required>.\nUpgrade: cargo install kanbus --locked --force\n```\n\nThat upgrade line is the **one** documented path (matches GETTING_STARTED cargo install). Do not add a second pip/curl variant in the error (parity). Mention both versions on the first line.\n\nFor unparseable `kanbus-version`:\n\n```\nkanbus-version is invalid: expected a single MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH value\n```\n\nFor unparseable running version:\n\n```\nKanbus CLI version '<raw>' cannot be compared with kanbus-version\n```\n\n## Gherkin (write first, watch it fail, then implement)\n\nAdd a dedicated feature file, e.g. `features/cli/kanbus_version.feature`. Observable behavior only. Suggested scenarios (names may be tightened, coverage may not be dropped):\n\n1. Older CLI vs newer project: project file `0.19.1`, running CLI `0.18.3` (or a required version **above** the test binary's parsed core, e.g. `99.0.0` against the real binary — prefer **not** inventing a production env-var if a high required version against the real `__version__` / `GIT_VERSION` proves the gate). If the test runner's version is `0.18.4`, requiring `0.19.1` or `99.0.0` is enough to fail. Also cover git-describe: if tests only see a clean cargo version, add a **unit-level** comparison table **and** at least one Gherkin that uses a required version the current binary cannot satisfy.\n2. Command exits nonzero **and** stderr contains both version strings **and** `cargo install kanbus --locked --force`.\n3. Compatible CLI: `kanbus-version` equal to the running core version (or `0.0.0`) then `kanbus doctor` / `kanbus list` succeed as today.\n4. Missing file: no version error; existing doctor-success scenario still passes.\n5. Git-describe style: if injecting the running version is required, do it **only in test doubles / cucumber world**, not a user-facing `KANBUS_CLI_VERSION` override. A small `compare_kanbus_versions(running, required)` function with table-driven unit tests in **both** languages is required for suffix cases.\n6. Invalid file contents fail before any \"ok\" doctor output.\n7. `kanbus doctor` on a too-new project fails with the version error (not `ok`).\n8. `kanbus --version` still succeeds even when `kanbus-version` is `99.0.0`.\n\nDo **not** add Python-only pytest that duplicate Gherkin. Dual-runtime: Python behave + Rust cucumber must both run the same feature. `tools/check_spec_parity.py` must stay green.\n\n## Implementation shape\n\n- One shared idea, two implementations: `python/src/kanbus/kanbus_version.py` and `rust/src/kanbus_version.rs` (or equivalent names). Public functions: parse, compare, `enforce_kanbus_version(root, running_version)`.\n- Call site: Python `cli()` group after parse, with skip list; Rust `run_from_args_with_output` after `Cli::try_parse_from` / `resolve_root`, before `maybe_prompt_project_repair` and `execute_command`.\n- Running version source: Python `__version__`; Rust `env!(\"GIT_VERSION\")` (same string `--version` prints). Do not invent a second version source.\n- No fallbacks. No \"warn and continue\". Title says warn; **acceptance is fail**.\n- No Mosquitto, no schema, no file-not-found after this error.\n\n## Docs\n\nUpdate operator docs so the file is a real contract:\n\n- `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` and/or `docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md`: what `kanbus-version` is, that the CLI refuses to run when older, and the upgrade command above.\n- Keep INSTALL/README consistent if they mention CLI prerequisites.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Writing `kanbus-version` from `kbs init` (unless a spec already requires it; it does not).\n- Migrating old projects.\n- Relaxing schema validation on purpose.\n- Changing wiki or doctor checks unrelated to version.\n\n## Quality\n\n- Smallest code that passes specs.\n- Sphinx on Python public functions; rustdoc on Rust public items.\n- No emojis. No debug leftovers. No commented-out code. No new `KANBUS_TEST_*` production knobs.\n- Commit on `cursor/cli-kanbus-version-gate-bf9f` from `develop`, push, do not open a PR.\n\n## Proof\n\nAfter implementation, run the new feature in both runtimes and the version unit tests. Record the command lines and that they pass in a Kanbus comment on this issue.\n",

./project/issues/tskl-5y8.3.json:4: "description": "Teams that want to deviate from FIFO defaults can do so via a sort_order block in .kanbus.yml. The primary API is a small set of named presets. Raw field sorting is available as an escape hatch. The schema applies per-status or per-category.\n\n## Rationale\n\nKanbus is opinionated but not a cage. Some contexts have legitimate reasons to sort differently — a backlog kept in deliberate priority order, for instance, is still a valid discipline if the team commits to maintaining it. The configuration system provides that flexibility while making the FIFO default the zero-config path.\n\nThe preset names are chosen to be self-documenting and to communicate the flow intent of each choice. A team choosing priority-first should know they are making a deliberate trade-off against FIFO visibility.\n\n## Presets\n\n- fifo — oldest created_at first (the default; equivalent to no configuration)\n- priority-first — sort by priority ascending (critical first), then by created_at ascending as a tiebreaker (FIFO within each priority band)\n- recently-updated — sort by updated_at descending; useful for a Blocked column where the team wants to see which blocked items were most recently touched\n\n## Configuration Schema\n\n sort_order:\n in_progress: priority-first\n categories:\n In progress: recently-updated\n backlog:\n - field: priority\n direction: asc\n - field: created_at\n direction: asc\n\nStatus-level configuration takes precedence over category-level configuration. Done-category columns ignore sort_order entirely (they are always last-updated descending).\n\nScenario: Preset fifo produces oldest-first ordering\n\nGiven sort_order for the Discovery status is set to the fifo preset\nWhen the user views the Discovery column\nThen issues are ordered oldest created_at first\nAnd this is identical to the default no-configuration behavior\n\nScenario: Preset priority-first sorts by priority then FIFO within each band\n\nGiven sort_order for the in_progress status is set to priority-first\nWhen the user views the In Progress column\nThen critical issues appear before high issues, which appear before medium, and so on\nAnd within each priority level issues are ordered oldest created_at first\n\nScenario: Preset recently-updated shows most recently touched items first\n\nGiven sort_order for the blocked status is set to recently-updated\nWhen the user views the Blocked column\nThen the issue with the most recent updated_at timestamp is at the top\n\nScenario: Category-level preset applies to all statuses in that category\n\nGiven sort_order categories sets In progress to priority-first\nAnd no status-level sort_order is set for blocked or in_progress\nWhen the user views the In Progress column and the Blocked column\nThen both columns sort by priority-first\n\nScenario: Status-level preset overrides category-level preset\n\nGiven sort_order categories sets In progress to priority-first\nAnd sort_order for the blocked status is set to recently-updated\nWhen the user views the Blocked column\nThen it sorts by recently-updated (not priority-first)\n\nScenario: Raw field sort is applied when specified\n\nGiven sort_order for backlog specifies a raw sort by priority asc then created_at asc\nWhen the user views the Backlog column\nThen issues are sorted by priority ascending and then by created_at ascending as a tiebreaker\n\nScenario: Done-category column ignores sort_order configuration\n\nGiven sort_order for the closed status is set to fifo\nWhen the user views the Done column\nThen it still sorts by last-updated descending\nAnd the sort_order configuration for closed is silently ignored\n\nScenario: An unrecognized preset name produces a validation error\n\nGiven sort_order for a status is set to an unrecognized preset name such as custom-magic\nWhen kbs validate is run\nThen an error is reported identifying the invalid preset name\nAnd the valid preset names are listed in the error message",

./project/issues/tskl-e7j.json:4: "description": "Add CLI commands and backend wiring to feature/focus a specific issue on the board via realtime messaging, including auto-focus on issue creation and agent-invoked focus.\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nThe current Kanbus architecture has a 15-second polling-based SSE system. This epic implements a real-time notification system using broadcast channels that reduces latency from 15 seconds to <100ms.\n\nKey insight: Once we build the socket-based notification infrastructure for the focus feature, we can extend it to ALL CRUD operations (create, update, delete), enabling the entire board to update with much lower latency.\n\n## Implementation Phases\n\n### Phase 1: Real-time Notification Infrastructure\n- Create notification_events.rs with NotificationEvent enum (IssueCreated, IssueUpdated, IssueDeleted, IssueFocused)\n- Extend console_local.rs with broadcast::channel for notifications\n- Create notification_publisher.rs to POST events to console server\n- Add SSE endpoint /api/events/realtime for streaming notifications\n\n### Phase 2: Hook CRUD Operations (see sub-tasks)\n- Hook issue_creation.rs, issue_update.rs, issue_delete.rs\n- Hook issue_comment.rs, dependencies.rs\n- Hook beads_write.rs for beads compatibility mode\n\n### Phase 3: Implement Focus Command\n- Add ConsoleCommands::Focus in cli.rs\n- Create focus handler that validates issue and publishes IssueFocused event\n- Add --focus flag to kbs create command for auto-focus on creation\n- Enable agents to invoke focus command\n\n### Phase 4: Frontend Integration\n- Add subscribeToNotifications() in api/client.ts\n- Handle notification events in App.tsx (focus, create, update, delete)\n- Add GSAP animations for visual feedback (see tskl-e7j.7)\n\n### Phase 5: Console Server Endpoints\n- POST /api/notifications - Receives events from CLI\n- GET /api/events/realtime - SSE stream for frontend\n- Use broadcast channel pattern like telemetry system\n\n## Critical Files\n\nBackend:\n- rust/src/bin/console_local.rs - Console server\n- rust/src/notification_events.rs (NEW)\n- rust/src/notification_publisher.rs (NEW)\n- rust/src/cli.rs - Add focus command\n\nFrontend:\n- apps/console/src/api/client.ts\n- apps/console/src/App.tsx\n- apps/console/src/components/IssueCard.tsx\n\n## Architecture Benefits\n\n1. Latency: 15 seconds → <100ms for all operations\n2. User Experience: Immediate feedback on all actions\n3. Agent Collaboration: Agents can direct human attention via focus\n4. Scalability: Broadcast channel supports multiple subscribers\n5. Backward Compatibility: Existing 15-second polling remains as fallback\n6. Extensibility: Easy to add new event types\n\n## Technical Considerations\n\n- Notification failures should not block CRUD operations\n- Broadcast channel buffer (256) prevents memory bloat\n- SSE connection auto-reconnects on failure\n- Event payload kept small (<5KB)\n- Console server binds to localhost only",

./project/issues/kbs-3b5cc3a5-1e3c-4121-89d8-9094df1f3fc6.json:4: "description": "## Implementation Plan: S3 Bridge Sync (No NAT)\n\n### Decision locked\nTwo-Lambda + S3 bridge. No Fargate, no ECS, no CodeBuild, no ALB, no NAT Gateway, no NAT instance, no VPC interface endpoints. ConsoleLambda stays on EFS unchanged. Git sync keeps working.\n\n### Why\nEFS forces compute into a VPC. VPC compute without NAT cannot reach GitHub (Lambda and CodeBuild ENIs get no public IP). The S3 bridge splits the job so no single compute needs both internet and EFS. S3 gateway endpoint is free (no hourly, no per-GB).\n\n### Architecture\n\n1. **Git Sync Lambda (non-VPC, new)** — consumes existing SyncQueue. Does git clone --no-checkout / git fetch / git reset --hard to /tmp, tars the repo, uploads tarball to S3. No VPC, no EFS, free internet.\n2. **S3 bucket (new)** — stores tenant repo tarballs keyed {account}/{project}/{sha}.tar.gz. Lifecycle: expire after 7 days. SSE-S3.\n3. **S3 gateway endpoint (free)** — vpc.add_gateway_endpoint so VPC-isolated Lambdas can read S3 without NAT.\n4. **EFS Writer Lambda (VPC, isolated, EFS, new)** — triggered by S3 object-created. Downloads tarball from S3 via gateway endpoint, extracts to EFS at /mnt/data/{account}/{project}/repo, publishes IoT cloud_sync_completed. VPC-isolated, no internet, no NAT.\n5. **ConsoleLambda (VPC, isolated, EFS, existing)** — unchanged. Reads EFS as today.\n6. **Delete** TenantSyncWorker Lambda + sync_worker.Dockerfile in the same changeset.\n7. **Leave alone:** webhook, token admin, MQTT authorizer (already not in VPC).\n\n### VPC\nnat_gateways=0. Public subnets (unused by compute) + PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnets (ConsoleLambda + EFS Writer Lambda + EFS). No PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS.\n\n### Files\n- infra/cloud/kanbus_cloud/cloud_stack.py — VPC/subnet/SG rework; ConsoleLambda to isolated; remove TenantSyncWorker; add S3 bucket + lifecycle; add S3 gateway endpoint; add Git Sync Lambda (non-VPC) + EFS Writer Lambda (VPC isolated EFS); wire SQS to Git Sync Lambda; wire S3 event to EFS Writer Lambda; update alarms/outputs.\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git_lib.py (new) — shared git + tarball helpers, no boto3, importable by tests.\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git.py (new) — Git Sync Lambda handler, non-VPC, SQS to S3.\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_git.Dockerfile (new) — git binary for Git Sync Lambda.\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_efs_writer.py (new) — EFS Writer Lambda handler, VPC isolated, S3 to EFS, IoT publish.\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_worker.py (delete)\n- infra/cloud/lambda/sync_worker.Dockerfile (delete)\n- infra/cloud/tests/test_no_nat_idle_cost.py (new) — zero NatGateway, zero ALB, zero ECS, TenantSyncWorker removed, Git Sync not in VPC, EFS Writer in VPC isolated with EFS, S3 gateway endpoint present, S3 bucket with lifecycle, SQS triggers Git Sync, S3 triggers EFS Writer.\n- infra/cloud/tests/test_ops_guardrails.py (modify) — alarm updates.\n- infra/cloud/tests/test_sync_handlers.py (modify) — tests for both new Lambdas.\n- infra/cloud/README.md, docs/CLOUD_OPS_RUNBOOK.md, docs/CLOUD_CONSOLE_RUNTIME.md, docs/CLOUD_LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md, scripts/cloud/validate_preacceptance.sh (modify) — sync path wording, no Fargate/CodeBuild mentions.\n\n### Cutover\nSingle atomic CDK deploy. Delete TenantSyncWorker + add two new Lambdas + S3 bucket + gateway endpoint in one changeset. One SQS consumer (Git Sync Lambda). One S3 trigger (EFS Writer Lambda). No dual actors.\n\n### Tests\n- test_zero_nat_gateways\n- test_zero_alb_nlb\n- test_zero_ecs_resources\n- test_tenant_sync_worker_removed\n- test_git_sync_lambda_not_in_vpc\n- test_efs_writer_lambda_in_vpc_isolated_with_efs\n- test_s3_gateway_endpoint_present\n- test_sync_bucket_lifecycle_seven_day_expiration\n- test_sqs_triggers_git_sync_lambda_only\n- test_s3_object_created_triggers_efs_writer_lambda\n- test_efs_security_group_restricts_nfs_to_console_and_writer\n\n### Staging smoke\nDeploy KanbusCloudFoundation (AWS_PROFILE=anthus, account 335163751677). No --all, no main. Verify: no NAT on VPC, /api/auth/bootstrap 200, ConsoleLambda logs appear, webhook to SQS to Git Sync to S3 to EFS Writer to EFS to IoT cloud_sync_completed. DLQ empty.\n\n### Out of scope\nFargate, ECS, CodeBuild, ALB/NLB, NAT Gateway, NAT instance, VPC interface endpoints, changes to console_lambda.rs, merge to main, cdk deploy --all.\n\n### Worktree\n/tmp/kanbus-kbs-3b5cc3-s3-bridge on branch fix/kbs-3b5cc3-s3-bridge from origin/develop. ./project/issues/kbs-87b6cede-720a-401e-8ae6-772a1039c7e3.json:4: "description": "## Problem\nThe hosted board at `/dev/anthus/kanbus/` works after a **manually signed** POST to `/internal/webhooks/github` with `X-Kanbus-Account` and `X-Kanbus-Project`.\n\nGitHub cannot send those headers. `AnthusAI/Kanbus` also has no webhook to KanbusCloudFoundation (only Amplify and Snyk). Accept tenant from the path, e.g. `POST /internal/webhooks/github/{account}/{project}`, same HMAC secret. Keep one way; do not also require headers.\n2. Gherkin first; Python and Rust parity if any CLI/docs mention the contract.\n3. Register a GitHub `push` webhook on AnthusAI/Kanbus to that URL with the Secrets Manager HMAC secret.\n4. Prove with a real GitHub delivery (or GitHub red\u00e9livery of a push) that `anthus/kanbus` syncs without custom headers.\n\n## DoD\n- GitHub can POST without `X-Kanbus-*` headers and still enqueue the right tenant.\n- Hook exists on AnthusAI/Kanbus pointing at KanbusCloudFoundation ingress.\n- A real push (or GitHub red\u00e9livery of a push) creates S3 `anthus/kanbus/{sha}.tar.gz` and `.synced.json`.\n- No NAT, no interface endpoints, no Fargate.\n\n## Out of scope\nWiki 404 on the hosted console. ./project/issues/tskl-5y8.json:4: "description": "Define how issues are ordered within each kanban column. Kanbus takes an opinionated stance on sorting grounded in Dan Vacanti's agile flow metrics: predictable, continuous-delivery workflows are built on FIFO discipline. The default sort orders are designed to make the right behavior the easy behavior — surfacing aging work, reinforcing pull-system discipline, and making flow problems visible without configuration.\n\n## Philosophy\n\nDan Vacanti's work on Actionable Agile Metrics establishes that predictable delivery depends on managing flow: keeping WIP low, processing work in order (FIFO), and making aging visible so teams respond before items become blockers. The default sort orders in Kanbus are chosen to make these principles the path of least resistance.\n\n**Done column**: Most-recently-completed work at the top. This is purely for human convenience — done work is done, and the person who just completed something should be able to confirm it immediately without scrolling. No configuration needed.\n\n**Active/waiting columns (Discovery, In Progress, Blocked, Backlog)**: Oldest item at the top by default. This is FIFO. It surfaces aging work. It creates natural pull pressure. It makes cycle time visible at a glance: if the top card has been there for weeks, the column has a problem. Letting teams re-sort these columns by priority or arbitrary fields is specifically the kind of customization that undermines flow visibility — so the default must be opinionated, and any deviation requires deliberate configuration.\n\n## Scope\n\n1. Done column always sorted by last-updated descending (most recently completed first). Not configurable per-column.\n2. Non-done columns default to created-at ascending (oldest first, pure FIFO).\n3. A sort_order configuration block in .kanbus.yml lets teams specify an ordered list of sort fields and directions per status (or per category).\n4. A narrow set of named presets (fifo, priority-first, recently-updated) covers the overwhelming majority of legitimate use cases and should be the primary API; raw field sorting is available for edge cases.\n5. The UI reflects whatever sort order is configured — no drag-to-reorder (drag-to-reorder defeats FIFO discipline and is deliberately not supported).",

./project/issues/kbs-b0a148ae-1b09-41df-9504-c6d3acc352c9.json:4: "description": "## User story\n\nAs an AI agent closing a Kanbus task, I want `kbs close <id> --comment \"...\"` to record the closing note and close the task in one command, so the completion record and status transition stay together.\n\n## Gherkin source of truth\n\nWrite shared executable scenarios before production code in the existing issue-close feature area. Run both behavior runners and capture their expected failure before implementation.\n\nScenarios must cover:\n- success: normal comment is appended, status becomes `closed`, and `closed_at` is set;\n- plain close: no comment and unchanged behavior;\n- empty/whitespace comment: fails before any mutation;\n- rejected close after a valid comment: comment remains and issue stays open;\n- lifecycle order: comment before/after hooks complete before close before/after hooks;\n- Beads-compatible project behavior;\n- Python/Rust matching persisted state, events, output, and exit status.\n\n## Implementation sequence\n\n1. Add `--comment <text>` to Python Click and Rust Clap close commands.\n2. Reuse normal comment behavior for validation, author, IDs, events, text-quality signals, hooks, and Beads compatibility.\n3. Execute comment first, then close. Preserve normal close output only; do not introduce an extra success line.\n4. Keep lower-level close domain functions status-transition-only; this is a CLI composite operation.\n5. Keep `close <id>` without `--comment` behavior unchanged.\n6. Ensure both binary help outputs expose the option.\n7. Verify existing reference docs, getting-started content, web docs, and agent guidance describe the delivered canonical command; edit only where accuracy needs it.\n\n## Required verification\n\nRun focused behavior/unit tests, Python quality gates, Rust quality gates, and `python tools/check_spec_parity.py`. Provide command output or concise results in the final Kanbus comment.\n\n## Delivery protocol\n\nWork on a feature branch from `develop`; open a PR targeting `develop`. Record milestone comments with:\n\n`Progress: …`\n`Evidence: …`\n`Next: …`\n`Risk/Blocker: …`\n\nUse Codex provenance on all comments. Close this story only after the PR-ready implementation has all specified checks green and the final comment records commit/PR plus exact verification commands.",

./project/issues/kbs-753e71c7-3af8-47a2-bfa5-a6678c81697d.json:4: "description": "## Objective\n\nBuild an optional Kanbus Issue Router that continuously dispatches eligible issue packages to coding-agent CLIs while preserving Kanbus as the durable source of truth. The router is a deterministic reconciliation loop, not an embedded AI agent loop.\n\nSuccess means accepted, merged value moving through the board with controlled work in progress. Agent utilization, dispatch count, and pull-request count are not success metrics.\n\n## Routing and package scope\n\nIssues opt into automation through either `agent-class:<name>` or `agent-provider:<name>` labels. Human assignees remain human-facing accountability and are never overwritten by execution ownership.\n\nA tagged parent is one routed work package and consumes one routed WIP slot. Its run may work within untagged descendants. The nearest explicit routing tag wins, so a tagged descendant begins a separate package and is excluded from the ancestor package scope.\n\nThe router validates a deterministic Definition of Ready before dispatch: configured pending status, valid routing target, no blocking dependency, bounded package scope, and project policy acceptance.\n\n## Deterministic flow policy\n\nWorkflow roles are configured explicitly per workflow: pending, active, review, blocked, and terminal. Recoverable active work and requested changes are dispatched before new work. New work is selected by the time it most recently entered the configured pending status, with creation time and issue ID as deterministic tie-breakers.\n\nThe router enforces configurable project-wide WIP, review WIP, agent-class, and provider-profile limits for its own starts. Project-wide counts include human and automated work in configured WIP statuses. Blocked and review work count by default. Manual Kanbus transitions may deliberately exceed the router limit.\n\nOpening a pull request moves the package to review; it does not complete the issue. Review consumes WIP and creates backpressure. Requested changes are re-dispatched ahead of pending work. Human approval and merge are required before terminal status.\n\n## Coordination, ownership, and recovery\n\nThe router asks Kanbus for transport-independent claims and uses the strongest configured provider: Git soft coordination, optional MQTT acceleration, and optional Mutex API hard arbitration. Git-only installations remain valid, and duplicate work remains possible under soft coordination.\n\nScheduling uses a short scheduler-epoch claim plus issue and capacity resources so cooperating routers cannot exceed configured limits when hard arbitration exists. Every run carries a claim ID and logical revision. Current-claim checks fence lifecycle transitions, accepted checkpoints, branch publication, pull-request creation, and result publication.\n\nExecution liveness and ownership staleness are separate clocks. Short leases detect dead processes and trigger bounded retry with backoff. Only structured progress or checkpoint reports attributed to the current claim reset the default 24-hour stale-ownership clock. Human comments and empty heartbeats do not.\n\nEach claim receives an isolated worktree and run-specific branch. The router owns checkpoints, push, and pull-request publication so an obsolete run cannot overwrite current work. Failed or stale runs preserve a router-owned WIP checkpoint; a takeover starts from the latest accepted checkpoint. After three retryable failures, the package moves to the configured blocked status with diagnostic history. Agent-class routes reconsider eligible providers on takeover; exact-provider routes remain pinned.\n\n## Agent and admission contracts\n\nAntigravity, Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code are first-class adapters. They implement one narrow structured contract for start, progress, checkpoint, cancellation, optional session resumption, usage telemetry, and final outcome. Provider capabilities remain explicit rather than hidden behind a false universal abstraction.\n\nThe router owns issue lifecycle. Agents may propose scoped descendant transitions through structured results; the router validates package scope, workflow policy, claim revision, and current issue revisions before applying them.\n\nVersion one uses deterministic fixed concurrency and an internal admission interface. The interface is designed for later built-in session-quota awareness, API-key budgets, token and cost accounting, and provider-specific capacity without assuming that all products use resetting sessions.\n\n## Review and forge integration\n\nA forge-independent reconciliation boundary observes pull-request creation, CI state, requested changes, approval, closure, and merge, with GitHub as the first implementation. External review state becomes auditable Kanbus events rather than a second queue.\n\nThe router provides deterministic pause, provider hold, package cancellation, and budget kill-switch controls. Parent-package size and runtime safeguards prevent unbounded context, change, and review units. Revision-cycle limits prevent endless implementation and review loops.\n\n## Success measures\n\nMeasure pending-to-merge lead time, review queue age, requested-change cycles, duplicate or obsolete runs, blocked-package age, cost per merged package, and post-merge failure or rollback rate.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Automatic merge in the initial system\n- LLM-based scheduling or an agent loop inside the router\n- A second durable task queue\n- Mandatory MQTT, Mutex API, or other cloud infrastructure\n- Universal enforcement of WIP limits on manual Kanbus transitions\n- Spotticus-style session-quota policy or monetary budget enforcement in version one",
./project/issues/kbs-2817309f-00bf-4b86-b45c-5e7c7ebd5c22.json:4: "description": "## Problem\n\nKanbus 0.23.0 does not declare a Rust minimum in `rust/Cargo.toml` and the repository has no Rust toolchain file or user-facing build prerequisite. On Cargo 1.81.0, a normal build fails inside a transitive dependency because `clap_lex 1.1.0` requires Edition 2024 support.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n`cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin kbs`\n\nEnvironment:\n\n- Kanbus commit `3c5dec99` / version 0.23.0\n- `rustc 1.81.0`\n- `cargo 1.81.0`\n\nObserved error:\n\n`feature edition2024 is required` while parsing the downloaded `clap_lex 1.1.0` manifest.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nKanbus should define one supported Rust toolchain contract. Building with an older toolchain should fail immediately with an actionable version requirement rather than a transitive-manifest error.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- The repository declares the supported Rust version in the canonical Cargo metadata or a pinned toolchain file.\n- Installation/build documentation states the same requirement.\n- CI verifies the declared minimum or intentionally uses the pinned version.\n- A build attempted with an older toolchain produces a clear actionable failure.\n- Release tooling reports the selected Rust toolchain.",
./project/issues/kbs-2817309f-00bf-4b86-b45c-5e7c7ebd5c22.json:17: "text": "# Implementation plan: declare and enforce Rust MSRV\n\nThis is the prescribed plan. Follow it. Do not invent extra product behavior. One toolchain contract, no fallbacks.\n\n## Intent\n\nAs a person building Kanbus from source, I want a single declared Rust version so that an old `rustc` fails immediately with an actionable requirement instead of a transitive-manifest error (`clap_lex` / `edition2024`).\n\n## Product contract (one way)\n\n1. **Canonical MSRV** is the stable compiler that current dependencies actually require. Edition 2024 (pulled by current `clap_lex`) is stable from **Rust 1.85**. Set **`rust-version = \"1.85\"`** in `rust/Cargo.toml` `[package]` unless you prove a *higher* floor is required by compiling the crate (then use that higher `X.Y` consistently everywhere).\n2. **Pin the same version** in a repo-root or `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel = \"1.85.0\"` or the chosen `X.Y.Z`). One pin. Developers and CI use that file. Do not leave CI on floating `stable` while Cargo claims 1.85.\n3. **Do not** \"fix\" the bug by pinning an older `clap_lex` so 1.81 still builds. That is a second supported toolchain. Forbidden.\n4. Building with an older toolchain must fail at Cargo's rust-version gate (`package rust-version` / `rustc < rust-version`), not inside a downloaded dependency manifest.\n\n## Docs (must match the pin)\n\nUpdate every user-facing build prerequisite that currently says only \"Rust toolchain (stable)\":\n\n- `INSTALL.md`\n- `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` / `GETTING_STARTED.md` if duplicated\n- `README.md` if it mentions the Rust toolchain\n- Any other install path you touch (`docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` only if it currently tells people to use unspecified stable)\n\nState the same number: **Rust 1.85 or newer** (or the chosen floor), and that `rust-toolchain.toml` pins CI and local `rustup`.\n\n## CI and release tooling\n\n- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `codeql.yml`: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` must install the **pinned** toolchain (the action honors `rust-toolchain.toml` if you stop overriding with anonymous stable, **or** pass `toolchain:` matching the pin). After checkout, `rustc --version` in the rust job should show the pin.\n- `tools/build_rust_release.py` already runs `rustc --version` / `cargo --version`. Keep that and make the printed output clearly include the selected toolchain (do not remove it). If the script does not echo those versions to the operator, it must.\n- Optional but preferred: a tiny CI step `cargo metadata --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --format-version 1` is enough; do **not** add a heavy matrix of old rustc unless it is cheap. The acceptance criterion \"CI verifies the declared minimum or intentionally uses the pinned version\" is satisfied by **building on the pin**, not by a second old-rust job (old-rust job would be nice but is extra). Prefer documenting that CI **is** the pin.\n\n## Gherkin / specs\n\nThis is a packaging/toolchain contract, not a `kbs list` behavior. Still specify what operators observe:\n\n- If you can express it in Gherkin without shelling out to a second rustc (usually you cannot in this repo's cucumber world), prefer **executable docs + a focused test** of whatever helper prints the toolchain.\n- Add Gherkin only if it is honest observable CLI behavior (for example a `kbs doctor` line that reports `rustc` is **out of scope** unless you already have doctor rustc checks — do **not** expand doctor).\n- Required: documentation files listed above contain the MSRV string; `Cargo.toml` has `rust-version`; `rust-toolchain.toml` exists.\n- Add a small unit or scripted check if one already exists for repo invariants; otherwise a `tools/` assertion is acceptable **only** if it is the one check and is run from documented quality gates. Prefer Cargo's own rust-version field as the enforcement mechanism.\n\nDo **not** add fake cucumber that claims `cargo build` ran rustc 1.81 in CI.\n\n## Quality\n\n- No emojis.\n- No leftover debug.\n- Dual-runtime Python/Rust **product** code is unchanged except docs/CI/Cargo (Python MSRV is unchanged).\n- Commit on `cursor/rust-msrv-pin-bf9f` from `develop`, push, do not open a PR.\n\n## Proof\n\nRecord `rg rust-version rust/Cargo.toml`, contents of `rust-toolchain.toml`, and a `cargo metadata` / `rustc --version` snippet in a comment on this issue.\n",

## Project management with Kanbus

Use Kanbus for task management.
Why: Kanbus task management is MANDATORY here; every task must live in Kanbus.
When: Create/update the Kanbus task before coding; close it only after the change lands.
How: See CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md for the Kanbus workflow, hierarchy, status rules, priorities, command examples, and the mistakes to avoid. Never inspect project/ or issue JSON directly (including with cat or jq); use Kanbus commands only.
Performance: Prefer kbs (Rust) when available; kanbus (Python) is equivalent but slower.
Warning: Editing project/ directly violates The Way. Do not read or write anything in project/; work only through Kanbus.
Git / PR policy: Rules for product-code commits, branch names, pull requests, and human approval live in this repository's AGENTS.md (outside this Kanbus section). CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md covers Kanbus board mechanics such as `kbs commit`; follow AGENTS.md for product code and git workflow.

## Right-now WIP (`kbs now`)

Agents can pull current board context on demand:

```bash
kbs now # whole-project WIP tree (default cap)
kbs now --list # flat list
kbs now --json --list # machine-readable flat list (includes priority)
kbs now kbs-abc # focused: issue and descendants
kbs now kbs-abc --list # focused flat list
```

Use scoped `kbs now <id>` when you are working a pinned epic or task. Whole-project reinjection after coding-agent context compaction is a separate hook pattern; see [docs/AGENT_COMPACTION_RIGHT_NOW.md](docs/AGENT_COMPACTION_RIGHT_NOW.md).

## System-wide kbs/kbsc install (agent PATH)

The agent environment only sees `/usr/local/bin` by default. To ensure `kbs` and `kbsc` are always available without PATH hacks, use the repo helper:

```bash
tools/install-system.sh
```

To avoid reinstalling after every build, use a one-time system-wide symlink:

```bash
tools/install-system.sh --mode symlink
```

This may require sudo once to create the links in `/usr/local/bin`. After that, rebuild with `cargo build --release` and the symlinks will pick up the new binaries automatically.

## Wiki Markus rendering

Kanbus wiki HTML uses [Markus](https://anthusai.github.io/Markus) (`anthus-markus`, import `markusmd`). **Do not `pip install markus`** — PyPI `markus` is Mozilla's metrics library and is unrelated.

- Rust `kbs`: built-in `wiki_markus` (no separate install)
- Python `kanbus`: `anthus-markus` from GitHub, installed via `pip install -e python`
- Smoke test: `kbs wiki render project/wiki/index.md --html | grep markus-document`

Full guide: [docs/WIKI_GUIDE.md](docs/WIKI_GUIDE.md#markus-renderer-not-pypi-markus).

## VideoML pipeline (Kanb.us)

The Kanb.us marketing site uses VideoML sources in `videos/`. The render and upload flow is centralized in root scripts.

Required environment variables:
- `VIDEOML_CLI` path to the VideoML CLI entry (e.g., `/path/to/videoml/cli/bin/vml.js`)
- `BABULUS_BUNDLE` path to the Babulus standard bundle JS

Node: The VideoML CLI requires Node 20+ (uses import attributes). Use `nvm use 20` or equivalent before running the render pipeline.

Local render + preview:
```bash
node scripts/render-videos.js
```
This bundles custom components, generates timelines, renders the intro MP4, and copies MP4/JPG assets into `apps/kanb.us/static/videos` for local preview. To preview on the Gatsby site, set:
```
GATSBY_VIDEOS_BASE_URL=/videos
```

Upload to CDN:
```bash
VIDEOS_BUCKET=<bucket-name> VIDEOS_PREFIX=videos node scripts/upload-videos.js
```
The upload script requires `VIDEOS_BUCKET` and `VIDEOS_PREFIX` and syncs MP4/JPG assets to S3. There is no fallback logic.

## Console board screenshots (agents)

When the user or Quality asks to **see the board**, capture it with `kbs console screenshot` (not a text `kbs list`). Set layout flags on the command so the PNG matches the ask; do not describe the board in prose when a screenshot can show it.

```bash
# Default: light mode, console default type filter, config-collapsed columns stay collapsed
kbs console screenshot

# Newsroom / pod board: every issue type, every column expanded (backlog, blocked, closed, etc.)
kbs console screenshot --view all --expand-all --output board.png

# Single-type views match the console tabs (initiatives, epics, issues)
kbs console screenshot --view epics --expand-all

# Expand or collapse specific status columns (status keys from .kanbus.yml)
kbs console screenshot --expand backlog --expand closed
kbs console screenshot --collapse in_progress
```

`--view all` uses the console `?type=all` filter (the "All" type selector). `--view initiatives|epics|issues` navigates to that tab path. Column expand/collapse is applied in the headless capture session (Playwright), not via deprecated `kbs console view` / `collapse-column` live-control commands.

If screenshot cannot express the requested layout, extend `kbs console screenshot` in Kanbus rather than substituting a textual board summary.

## Console UI Control (deprecated live-control commands)

When the user is actively watching the Kanbus console UI (typically at http://localhost:4242), you can programmatically control the interface to guide their attention. These commands use real-time socket+SSE notifications with sub-100ms latency.

### Available Commands

**Focus on an issue** - Immediately highlights an issue and opens it in the detail panel, filtering the board to show only that issue and its descendants:
```bash
kbs console focus <issue-id>
```

**Reload the page** - Triggers an immediate page reload in the browser, useful after frontend changes:
```bash
kbs console reload
```

This enables self-iteration on frontend issues: after rebuilding the frontend (`cd apps/console && npm run build`), use `kbs console reload` to instantly test changes without manual browser refresh.

### When to Use UI Control

Use `kbs console focus` proactively when:
- **After creating important issues**: Direct attention to new epics or critical tasks
- **After significant updates**: Show the user changes you've made
- **During collaborative work**: Coordinate by showing what you're working on
- **To provide context**: Help the user understand relationships between issues

### Example Workflows

After creating a new epic with sub-tasks:
```bash
kbs create "Implement authentication" --type epic
# Creates tskl-abc
kbs create "Add login form" --parent tskl-abc --type task
kbs create "Add JWT tokens" --parent tskl-abc --type task
kbs console focus tskl-abc # Show the epic and all sub-tasks
```

When starting work on a task:
```bash
kbs update tskl-xyz --status in_progress --assignee agent
kbs console focus tskl-xyz # Show what you're working on
```

After completing a complex change:
```bash
kbs close tskl-xyz
kbs console focus tskl-abc # Show the parent epic with updated status
```

### Future Commands (tskl-m59)

Additional UI control commands are planned but not yet implemented:
- `kbs console unfocus` - Clear focus filter
- `kbs console view <initiatives|epics|issues>` - Switch view modes
- `kbs console search <query>` - Set search query
- `kbs console maximize` - Maximize detail panel
- `kbs console close-detail` - Close detail panel
- `kbs console settings mode <light|dark>` - Control appearance
- `kbs console column collapse <name>` - Collapse board columns

Check `kbs show tskl-m59` for implementation status.
